purpose: Rotating upstream update-check state. Each entry records the commit the local copies were verified against, so a later run starts from a real baseline instead of re-deriving one, and can pick the sources that have waited longest.
baseline_method: Every local file is compared to the upstream tree by git blob SHA. 'identical' therefore means the local copy is exactly verified_commit, not merely similar to it.

duplicate_skill_md_groups.what: Groups whose SKILL.md is byte-identical. Most come from the VoltAgent/awesome-agent-skills mass import re-adding skills that were already present under an --owner suffix. No group is a whole-directory duplicate: in almost every case one side carries supporting files the other lacks, so the more complete side has to be picked per group rather than by rule.

unmatched_candidates.what: Skills whose upstream directory exists but where not a single file matches by blob SHA. Each one is either a wholesale upstream rewrite worth taking or a coincidental same-name skill in an unrelated repository, where applying the update would destroy the local skill. Blob SHAs cannot tell those apart.
unmatched_candidates.triage: Run `tools/check-upstream.py <repo> --probe-frontmatter`. It reads the upstream SKILL.md and compares `name` and `description` to the local ones, and records the verdict under `checked[repo].frontmatter_probe`. `name-and-description-match` is strong evidence of the same skill; `name-differs` proves a collision and the update must not be applied. `local_files: 1` marks a single-file skill, which lands in this status whenever its one file changes at all, because one changed file leaves zero matched files. Two of the four updates applied on 2026-08-23 were found this way.
